head: dc0b9d5
target: Ship the repo as one plugin that Claude Code, Droid, and Codex each install, so every clone of an opted-in repo keeps its gate and agents cannot bypass it.
incidental: The selftest: moved to the repo root, run with isolated HOME and git config, and extended to cover the new hooks
Plugin metadata values: names, owner, version, and repository link
The guard's command parsing and its list of shell tool names
The installer's per-tool subcommands, its update fallback, and its source override flag
The gate's own sync and install commands, unchanged by this change; only the new tests exercise them

questions.prompt: Why does one plugin file set serve Claude Code, Droid, and Codex, instead of one package per tool?

options.label: All three tools read the same plugin folder and hook definitions.
Each tool runs the same plugin install command.
Each tool needs its own rewritten copy of the plugin folder.
Claude Code shares its installed plugins with the other two.

key_points: All three tools read the same plugin folder and hook definitions, so one file set serves all three.
The per-tool work lives in the installer, which installs into every tool it finds on the machine.

questions.prompt: A teammate clones a repo that opted into the gate and never runs the installer. How does their clone end up blocking unquizzed pushes?
key_points: The opt-in marker is a tracked file, so every clone carries it.
At session start, the plugin's hook syncs the clone: it installs the missing push hook and puts the gate command on PATH.
In repos that did not opt in, the session-start hook says nothing.
The session-start hook never fails the session.

questions.prompt: The push hook alone cannot stop an agent. How can an agent still get an unquizzed push through?

options.label: Push with the hook skipped, or point git at another hook path.
Delete the gate's records, so the hook has nothing to check.
Push a new branch the hook was never told to watch.
Skip the commit check, since the push gate hangs off it.

key_points: The agent can push with the push hook skipped, or point git at another hook path.
The guard that runs before each agent command denies both moves.
Skipping the gate stays the human's call, never the agent's.

questions.prompt: The installer has trusted the plugin's hooks in Codex. What later change makes Codex skip them again, and what fixes it?
key_points: Codex runs a plugin's hooks only when it trusts their definition hash.
A changed hook definition gets a new hash, so Codex skips it until it is trusted again.
Re-running the trust step, or approving in Codex, restores trust.

questions.prompt: A new teammate clones an opted-in repo on a machine the installer already set up for Codex. Which of these hold for their first session?

options.label: The clone starts with no push hook; session start installs it.
Their agent cannot get an unquizzed push through.
They must run the installer in the new clone first.
Codex asks them to approve the plugin's hooks again.

key_points: The clone carries the opt-in marker, so session start installs the missing push hook.
The push hook blocks any unquizzed commit, and the guard denies the agent's bypasses.
The installer already trusted the hooks in Codex, so no approval is asked again.
